scenarios.name: export-dynamic-batch-and-verify
scenarios.rationale: Both call model.eval(), use named inputs/outputs, pin opset_version, and compare onnxruntime against PyTorch with np.testing.assert_allclose on float32 input. B covers both exporter paths: dynamic_shapes with torch.export.Dim for the dynamo exporter and dynamic_axes with dynamo=False for the legacy one. A shows only dynamic_axes without dynamo=False, so on the PyTorch 2.9+ default dynamo exporter it is not the explicit legacy path the rubric requires, and it never mentions dynamo=False. A's verification loop over several batch sizes is more thorough.

scenarios.name: gpu-session-provider-fallback
scenarios.rationale: A states the onnxruntime-gpu install with the never-both warning, filters providers against get_available_providers() and feeds a float32 array via session.run(None, ...); B has the same code but only says to install one package at a time and shows the CPU package as an alternative, which is weaker on the 'never both' requirement, and it also suggests onnxruntime-gpu works everywhere, which departs from the rubric's install guidance.

scenarios.name: quantize-and-prepare-mobile
scenarios.rationale: Both use quantize_dynamic with QInt8 and the convert_onnx_models_to_ort module command; B explicitly says conv nets need quantize_static with calibration and explicitly states the Python function does not exist, and it stresses comparing accuracy on real data, while A covers static quantization in more depth but less directly ties dynamic to MatMul/Linear and its accuracy check is on holdout data (acceptable) without the explicit 'not a Python function' note.
